newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GENERALE BANK RAISES RETAILER GIB TO HOLD.
newsitem.headline: GENERALE BANK RAISES RETAILER GIB TO HOLD.

text.p: Generale Bank said in a research note published on Wednesday it was upgrading shares in Belgian retailer GIB to speculative 'hold' from 'sell'.
The bank said it expected GIB to take "concrete (and maybe energetic) measures to eventually put net current results in line with sales in the coming months."

"We see GIB as a turnaround company for which 1998 results could prove higher than the current consensus (101 francs per share, or plus 13 percent)," it said. "In addition we believe that more speculation could arise along with better fundamentals as Cobepa could wish to step out of GIB."
Holding company Cobepa is currently the largest shareholder in GIB with 17.8 percent.

"All in all we think GIB deserves a better rating, albeit from a somewhat speculative point of view," it said. The bank added it expected GIB to tell shareholders on Wednesday that it would need to go further in the improvement of profitability.
The retailer's results have been volatile over the past five years. GIB profit per share was 100 francs in 1996, reversing 1995's loss of 130.
GIB said earlier this week it planned to invest seven billion francs in 1997 on restructuring and development.
It said the cash would be used partly to strengthen its commercial agreement with France's Promodes and consolidate the recovery of Florida-based DIY chain Scotty's.

The money would also be used to develop European DIY activities and continue the expansion and improve competitiveness of its Quick hamburger restaurant network. GIB invested a total 5.9 billion francs in 1996.
GIB is streamlining its Belgian GB, Nopri and Unic supermarket outlets to create better synergies. The stores would collaborate more closely on purchasing and logistics as well as store branding.
BBL brokerage Vermeulen Raemdonck said in its monthly review of the Belgian market GIB was a 'hold'. The share had gained 1.29 percent in May, but over the past three months it shed 3.09 percent.
On a broadly weaker Brussels bourse it was up 5 francs at 1,700 francs at 1220 GMT, having hit a 1997 high of 1,715 francs in line with general market bullishness on June 13.
